builds.name: I refuse to yield!
builds.desc: Loyal to his recognition as the original Fire Emblem unit, the Hero-King aims to retake the throne for all! This build aims to harmonize Null Follow-Up 3 with the Hero-King's speed oriented imbuement. Null Follow-Up 3 prevents foes who have skills like Quick Reposte or Brash Assault from doubling on Marth. This results in a typical speed check, one which the Hero-King excels at given his relatively high speed stat. This is furthered by his weapon, the Exalted Falchion, and Fire Emblem which, after a battle, adds at least +8 to Marth's speeds stats. Skills like Swift Sparrow add more to the speed and attack on player phases to ensure Marth doubles opponents without getting doubled back and Odd Atk Wave 3 along with +Spd ivs allow the Hero-King to seal speed and damage output dominance against most units. With all his speed and buffing prowess, Flashing Blade 3 combined with his almost guaranteed double attacks allows Fire Emblem to activate nearly every engagement.

builds.name: Speed Demon Marth
builds.desc:
Marth is a speedy swordsman. Why not try to build his kit to go even faster?
Making his asset/boon +Spd will keep his base Spd 42 when he's unmerged, which is excellent, guaranteeing follow-up attacks against most of the units. As for a flaw/bane, -HP can get Marth's Spurn threshold lower, causing it to proc its secondary effect faster, but it's also a -4 superbane. (just merge him dummy it's not hard /s)
Exalted Falchion grants Marth an extra 3 Spd and a built-in Bonus Doubler 3, which will automatically work whenever his Special, Fire Emblem, is activated, essentially giving him an additional +8 to every stat. Exalted Falchion can work even better if you have allies running Opening/Gap skills, especially Atk Opening 3, Spd Opening 3, or Atk/Spd Gap 3.
Atk/Spd Push 4 gives Marth +7 to his Atk and Spd almost all the time, albeit at a penalty of 5 HP after combat if he attacked. This is a better option compared to Fury 4, which only gives him +4 to his stats at the cost of 8 HP, or Life and Death 4, which increases his Atk and Spd but reduces his bulk, which isn't really the best idea for him. The eventual build up of damage from Atk/Spd Push can drop his HP down to less than 75%, which is low enough for Spurn's damage bonus to activate. Alternatively, you can run Atk/Spd Bond 4, which would be a quick upgrade to his base kit and nullify any penalties on Marth, or Atk/Spd Solo 4, both of which giving Marth the +7 to Atk and Spd without the damage penalty, and replacing the HP condition to an ally-dependent condition.
Spurn 3, Close Call 3, or Repel 3 are pivotal skills in any Spd-centered unit, and Marth is barely an exception. While Binding Shield is Marth's personal B passive and is a very powerful skill against Dragon units, it can be rendered useless when no Dragon units are found on a map. One of the Evasion skills is a lot better in terms of versatility, and Marth can get a lot of mileage out of one of these skills. I personally recommend Spurn out of the three, as Close Call and Repel only work on Player Phase, as well as the fact that Atk/Spd Push's damage helps Marth proc Spurn's secondary effect.
For C passives, two of the best options are Joint Drive Atk and Joint Drive Spd; these grant Marth a guaranteed boost to either Atk or Spd, and he benefits from either. You could run one of the Joint Drives on him and then another on a different unit; it's up to how you want to play. If you want more visible buffs for Marth to double, you can look at the Joint Hone, Odd/Even Wave, or Rouse/Oath skill families.
For his Seal, Spd/Res Solo 3 gives +6 to both his best and worst stats. That +6 Res granted by Spd/Res Solo can help patch up Marth's fights against mages or dragons; especially the latter, if you ever find yourself short on damage facing a blue dragon unit. You can also run Flashing Blade 3 for faster Fire Emblem activations, but the cooldown is already fairly low and isn't really a big deal unless your opponent has Guard or a Tier 4 Stance skill.
I run my S-Supported Marth on a team with Male Robin running Tactical Bolt with his Skill refine for a free +4 visible buff to all stats, Legendary Hector, where he provides a free -1 Special cooldown to everyone thanks to Ostia's Pulse, and Hot Spring Sakura running Spd Opening 3 for another +2 to Marth's Speed. Sakura's Grandscratcher+ can also potentially give Marth another -1 charge on turn 1, giving him Fire Emblem at the very start of combat.
